name: Striped Bass
diet: Menhaden and other small fish, crabs
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Silver body with 7 to 8 dark stripes running from head to tail
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Summer Flounder (Fluke)
id_tips: Flat body with both eyes on the left side; brown with eye-like spots
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Bluefish
id_tips: Blue-green back, silver sides, and a large jaw with sharp teeth
what_to_do: Handle carefully because of the sharp teeth.

name: Atlantic Sturgeon
best_time: Any time; feeds along the bottom
id_tips: Long body with rows of bony plates, a shark-like tail, and whisker-like barbels
what_to_do: Release immediately with as little handling as possible. It is illegal to keep.

name: Red Lionfish
id_tips: Red and white stripes with long, fan-like spines
what_to_do: The spines are venomous, so do not touch. Removal is encouraged; report sightings to your state wildlife agency.

name: Atlantic Cod
best_time: Day and night near the bottom
habitat: Rocky and gravel bottoms in cold water
id_tips: Three dorsal fins, a chin barbel, and a pale line along the side
what_to_do: The population in New England is low. Check current rules before fishing.

name: European Green Crab
habitat: Tide pools, salt marshes, and mudflats
id_tips: Five spines on each side of the shell behind the eyes; color varies and is not always green
what_to_do: Never move it or release it somewhere else. Report sightings where it is new.

name: North Atlantic Right Whale
diet: Tiny copepods filtered from the water
habitat: Cape Cod Bay and coastal waters
id_tips: Dark body with no dorsal fin, rough white patches on the head, and a V-shaped blow
what_to_do: Federal law requires staying at least 500 yards away.

name: Common Snook
id_tips: Sleek silver body with a bold black line along the side and a sloped forehead
what_to_do: Sensitive to cold. Follow Florida seasons and slot limits.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Tarpon
id_tips: Large silver scales, an upturned mouth, and a long last ray on the dorsal fin
what_to_do: Mostly caught and released. Keep large fish in the water when possible.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Smalltooth Sawfish
best_time: Any time; often in shallow water
id_tips: Flat, shark-like body with a long, flat snout lined with teeth on both sides
what_to_do: Never keep one. Leave it in the water, cut the line as close to the hook as is safe, and report the encounter.

name: Red Drum (Redfish)
best_time: Morning and evening on moving tides
id_tips: Copper-bronze body with one or more black spots near the tail
what_to_do: Follow local slot limits.

name: Spotted Seatrout
id_tips: Silvery-gray with scattered black spots on the back and tail; two large front teeth
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Kemp's Ridley Sea Turtle
habitat: Shallow Gulf waters, bays, and nesting beaches
id_tips: The smallest sea turtle, with a round gray-olive shell
what_to_do: Do not approach or touch. Report nesting or stranded turtles to local authorities.

name: California Halibut
habitat: Sandy bottoms near shore and in bays
id_tips: Flat body that can have eyes on either side; a large mouth that reaches past the eye
what_to_do: Follow California size limits.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Kelp Bass (Calico Bass)
id_tips: Olive-brown body with pale blotches in a calico pattern
what_to_do: Follow California size and bag limits.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Garibaldi
id_tips: Bright orange all over; young fish have blue spots
what_to_do: California's state marine fish. It is illegal to take one.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Devilweed (invasive seaweed)
diet: Makes its own food through photosynthesis
id_tips: Brown seaweed with small air bladders and fern-like leaves; can form thick mats
what_to_do: Do not move it between areas. Clean boats and gear before leaving.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Southern Sea Otter
diet: Sea urchins, crabs, clams, and snails
id_tips: Small furry marine mammal that floats on its back and often uses rocks as tools
what_to_do: Give plenty of space. If an otter changes what it is doing because of you, you are too close.

name: Leopard Shark
best_time: Daytime in shallow water, especially on rising tides
diet: Crabs, clams, worms, and small fish
habitat: Shallow bays, sandy flats, and near kelp
id_tips: Slim gray shark with dark saddle bars and spots along the back
what_to_do: Harmless to people. Follow size limits.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Lingcod
id_tips: Large head and mouth with sharp teeth; mottled brown-gray body
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits.
source: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Black Rockfish
diet: Small fish, krill, and crab larvae
id_tips: Dark gray to black body with a pale belly and a spiny dorsal fin
what_to_do: Fish brought up from deep water can be injured by the pressure change. Use a descending device when releasing.
source: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Dungeness Crab
diet: Clams, small crabs, worms, and fish
id_tips: Purple-brown shell with white-tipped claws
what_to_do: Only males of legal size may be kept. Check current seasons.
source: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: Hawaiian Monk Seal
best_time: Rests on beaches by day, feeds at night
id_tips: Gray-brown seal with no visible ear flaps; often rests on the sand
what_to_do: Stay at least 50 feet away, and 150 feet from a mother with a pup.

name: Green Sea Turtle (Honu)
habitat: Reefs, seagrass beds, and shallow coastal waters
id_tips: Smooth oval shell and a small rounded head with a blunt beak
what_to_do: Stay at least 10 feet away. Never touch or feed.

name: Reef Triggerfish (Humuhumunukunukuapuaa)
diet: Small invertebrates, algae, and sea urchins
id_tips: Hawaii's state fish; a black wedge-shaped band on the side and yellow lines near the mouth
what_to_do: Enjoy watching and do not touch the reef.

name: Roi (Peacock Grouper)
id_tips: Dark brown body covered in small blue spots
what_to_do: Introduced to Hawaii in the 1950s. It can carry ciguatera toxin, so eating it is not recommended.

name: Barracuda
id_tips: Large sliver body with sharp teeth and slim body
what_to_do: Handle carefully because of the sharp teeth.

name: Sheepshead
id_tips: Distinct black and white stripes with human like teeth
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Cobia
habitat: Reefs, seagrass beds, and shallow coastal waters
id_tips: Dark brown body with one dorsal fin and horizontal black and white stripes
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Peacock Flounder
habitat: Sandy bottoms near shore and in bays
id_tips: Flat oval body with blue rings and able to change colors
what_to_do: Never move it or release it somewhere else. Report sightings where it is new.

name: Spot
best_time: Any time; feeds along the bottom
id_tips: One dark spot right behind the gill plate
what_to_do: Follow local bag limit

name: Yellowtail Amberjack
id_tips: Bright yellow tail long body and a brassy yellow stripe running down its back
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits.

name: Leatherback Sea Turtle
id_tips: Massive sized turtle with rubbery shell with seven raised ridges running lengthwise
what_to_do: Stay at least 150 ft away

name: Blue Crab
best_time: Any time; often in shallow water
id_tips: Olive green shell, paddle shaped rear legs, and bright red or blue claws
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Cownose Ray
habitat: Shallow bays, sandy flats, and near kelp
id_tips: Two distinctive cow like snout and plain brown kite shaped body
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits as well as looking out for the venomous barb at the end

name: Bonefish
habitat: Shallow bays, sandy flats, and near kelp
id_tips: A silvery long torpedo shaped white body with a pig shaped snout
what_to_do: Safely unhook it and release it or follow local size and bag limit

name: King Salmon
habitat: Shallow bays, sandy flats, and near kelp
id_tips: Black spots of both sides of the tail and black color around the fishes gums
what_to_do: Follow Alaska laws about size and bag limit

name: Red snapper
id_tips: Red oval shape body, red eyes, with big mouth and teeth
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Gag Grouper
id_tips: Gray or brown colored body with black markings and a large Jaw
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits as well as the bag limit

name: King Mackerel
id_tips: Long slandered body with a deep forked shaped tail
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Blacktip Shark
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Gray long body with black tip of the fins especially on the pectoral fin
what_to_do: Release immediately with as little handling as possible.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Spanish Mackerel
id_tips: Silver body with yellowish spots and a streamlined shape.
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Bull Shark
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Broad blunt snout, stocky body and small eyes.
what_to_do: Release immediately with as little handling as possible.

name: Walleye Pollock
id_tips: Elongated body, dark back and pale sides.
what_to_do: Follow Alaska laws about size and bag limit

name: Tripletail
id_tips: Deep body, brown coloration, and three tail-like fins.
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Black Drum
id_tips: Dark gray to black body, large scales, and chin barbels.
what_to_do: Keep or release according to local size and bag limits.

name: Florida Pompano
diet: Sea urchins, crabs, clams, and snails
id_tips: Tall, flattened silver body with dark fins and deeply forked tail.
what_to_do: Keep or release according to local size and bag limits.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Wahoo
id_tips: Long narrow body, sharp teeth, blue-green back, and distinctive vertical blue bars.
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Blackfin Tuna
id_tips: Dark blue-black back, silver sides, and relatively short pectoral fins.
what_to_do: Keep or release according to local size and bag limits.

name: Tautog
id_tips: Thick dark body, blunt head, large teeth.
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits as well as the bag limit

name: Scup
diet: Clams, small crabs, worms, and fish
id_tips: Silver body with darker back and small mouth.
what_to_do: Follow local seasons and size limits

name: Atlantic croaker
id_tips: Silver-gray body with faint dark markings and chin barbels
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Pacific Sanddab
id_tips: Flat body with both eyes on one side.
what_to_do: Follow local bag limit
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: California Scorpionfish
id_tips: Mottled reddish-brown body, large head, spiny fins.
what_to_do: Handle carefully because of sharp spines; follow local rules.

name: Arctic Grayling
id_tips: Large sail-like dorsal fin with colorful spots.
what_to_do: Follow Alaska fishing regulations.

name: Kelp Greenling
id_tips: Long body with mottled green, brown, or reddish coloration.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.
source: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

name: California Corbina
id_tips: Silver-gray body and pointed dorsal fin.
what_to_do: Follow California regulations.

name: Cabezon
id_tips: Large head, wide mouth, mottled body.
what_to_do: Check local regulations before keeping.

name: Weakfish
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Silver body with dark spots on back and fins.
what_to_do: Follow current local regulations.

name: Giant Trevally
id_tips: Large muscular body, dark coloration, powerful tail.
what_to_do: Follow Hawaii regulations; handle carefully.

name: Pacific Halibut
id_tips: Very large flat body with both eyes on one side.
what_to_do: Follow current halibut regulations.

name: Hogfish
id_tips: Long snout, reddish-orange fins, elongated body.
what_to_do: Follow current regulations.

name: Bonnethead Shark
id_tips: Shovel-shaped head and small body.
what_to_do: Follow shark regulations; release carefully.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Nurse Shark
id_tips: Broad flat head, small eyes, barbels around mouth.
what_to_do: Avoid unnecessary handling; release carefully.

name: Greater Amberjack
id_tips: Long body with amber stripe through the eye.
what_to_do: Check current size and possession limits.

name: Vermilion Snapper
id_tips: Reddish body with pinkish sides and pointed snout.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.

name: Lane Snapper
id_tips: Pinkish-red body with yellow stripes and dark spot.
what_to_do: Follow current regulations.

name: Mangrove Snapper
id_tips: Gray body, dark lateral line, reddish fins.
what_to_do: Follow local size and bag limits.

name: Jack Crevalle
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Thick body, yellowish fins, dark spot near gill cover.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.

name: Permit
diet: Crabs, clams, worms, and small fish
habitat: Shallow bays, sandy flats, and near kelp
id_tips: Tall, flattened silver body and deeply forked tail.
what_to_do: Follow current regulations.

name: Gray Triggerfish
diet: Small invertebrates, algae, and sea urchins
id_tips: Deep compressed body and prominent dorsal spines.
what_to_do: Follow current regulations.

name: Southern Stingray
best_time: Any time; feeds along the bottom
id_tips: Diamond-shaped body and long whip-like tail.
what_to_do: Avoid stepping on it; release carefully.

name: Spadefish
best_time: Any time; often in shallow water
id_tips: Tall silver body with several dark vertical bands.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.

name: Lemon Shark
habitat: Bays, inlets, and the surf zone
id_tips: Yellowish-brown body and broad snout.
what_to_do: Follow shark regulations; release carefully.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Atlantic Sharpnose Shark
best_time: Any time; feeds along the bottom
id_tips: Slim body, pointed snout, gray back and white underside.
what_to_do: Follow current shark regulations.
source: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission

name: Ladyfish
best_time: Any time; often in shallow water
id_tips: Long slender silver body and deeply forked tail.
what_to_do: Often released; follow local regulations.

name: Almaco Jack
id_tips: Deep-bodied jack with dark stripe through the eye.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.

name: Southern Kingfish
id_tips: Slender silver body with darker back and chin barbels.
what_to_do: Follow local regulations.

name: Sablefish
id_tips: Dark gray-black body, smooth skin, two dorsal fins.
what_to_do: Follow current Alaska/Pacific regulations.
